text: High intracellular concentrations of the second messenger cyclic di-GMP (c-di-GMP) bias a bacterium toward which lifestyle?
choices: Rapid planktonic swimming with frequent runs
explanation: c-di-GMP is the master lifestyle-decision molecule: high levels promote sessile biofilm behavior (matrix synthesis, adhesion, suppressed motility), while low levels favor motile planktonic swimming, so option 0 describes the low-c-di-GMP state. Sporulation (option 2) is governed by the Spo0A phosphorelay, and lytic replication (option 3) is a bacteriophage program, neither controlled by c-di-GMP.
